attempts.summary: Bootstrapped a fresh three-member etcd 3.4.30 cluster (node1, node2, node3) via apt, seeded application keys, then simulated permanent loss of the node3 member (stopped etcd, irrecoverably deleted its data dir). Cluster maintained quorum on node1+node2 throughout the outage and continued to serve writes. Removed the dead member (ba8dfe0c41fd56ec) from the cluster, added a fresh replacement member for node3 (41e5d7e30b10e80d), reconfigured node3 with a clean data dir and ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_STATE=existing, and started it — it joined the cluster and synced all data. Verified 3/3 healthy members and all application keys intact (including a key written during the node3 outage). Then ran the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id + etcd health baseline, rebooted one node at a time via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and confirmed etcd + cluster membership + application keys recovered fully before moving to the next node. Final state: 3/3 etcd members healthy, all application keys present.
